                   21          1.      PURPOSE
                   22          This Order will govern discovery of electronically stored information (“ESI”) in this case
                   23   as a supplement to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, this Court’s Guidelines for the Discovery
                   24   of Electronically Stored Information, and any other applicable orders and rules. Nothing in this
                   25   Order shall be interpreted to require disclosure of irrelevant information or relevant information
                   26   protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, or any other applicable privilege
                   27   or immunity. The parties do not waive any objections as to the production, discoverability,
                   28   admissibility, or confidentiality of documents and ESI.

                    1          2.      COOPERATION
                    2          The parties are aware of the importance the Court places on cooperation and commit to
                    3   cooperate in good faith throughout the matter consistent with this Court’s Guidelines for the
                    4   Discovery of ESI.
                    5          3.      LIAISON
                    6          The parties have identified liaisons to each other who are and will be knowledgeable about
                    7   and responsible for discussing their respective ESI. Each e-discovery liaison will be, or have access
                    8   to those who are, knowledgeable about the technical aspects of e-discovery, including the location,
                    9   nature, accessibility, format, collection, search methodologies, and production of ESI in this matter.
                   10   The parties will rely on the liaisons, as needed, to confer about ESI and to help resolve disputes
                   11   without court intervention.
                   12          Tallied appoints Linda Vu as its discovery liaison.
                   13          Panacea appoints Nicole Blake as its discovery liaison.
                   14          4.      PRESERVATION
                   15          The parties have discussed their preservation obligations and needs and agree that
                   16   preservation of potentially relevant ESI will be reasonable and proportionate. To reduce the costs
                   17   and burdens of preservation and to ensure proper ESI is preserved, the parties agree that:
                   18                  a)      The parties have exchanged or will exchange a list of the types of ESI they
                   19                          believe should be preserved and the custodians, or general job titles or
                   20                          descriptions of custodians, for whom they believe ESI should be preserved,
                   21                          e.g., “HR head,” “scientist,” and “marketing manager.” The parties shall add
                   22                          or remove custodians as reasonably necessary.
                   23                  b)      These data sources are not reasonably accessible because of undue burden
                   24                          or cost pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(2)(B) and ESI from these sources
                   25                          will be preserved but not searched, reviewed, or produced: backup systems
                   26                          and/or tapes; and systems no longer in use that cannot be accessed;
                   27

                    2                          regarding other data upon request that (a) could contain relevant information

                    4          5.      SEARCH
                    5          The parties agree that in responding to an initial Fed. R. Civ. P. 34 request, or earlier if
                    6   appropriate, they will meet and confer about the methods being used to search ESI in order to
                    7   identify ESI that is subject to production in discovery and filter out ESI that is not subject to
                    8   discovery. The receiving party may suggest revisions to these methods, which shall be considered
                    9   in good faith by the producing party.
                   10          6.      PRODUCTION FORMATS
                   11          The parties agree to produce documents in searchable PDF, TIFF, native (for XLS files)
                   12   and/or a combination thereof file formats. If particular documents warrant a different format, the
                   13   parties will cooperate to arrange for the mutually acceptable production of such documents. The
                   14   parties agree, to the extent practicable, not to materially degrade the searchability of documents as
                   15   part of the document production process.
                   16          7.      PHASING
                   17          When a party propounds discovery requests pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 34, the parties agree
                   18   to phase the production of ESI. The initial production of ESI from Tallied shall be from the
                   19   following Tallied custodians: Sunil Singh and Venkat (Vinni) Bala.     Panacea will similarly make
                   20   an initial ESI production from 2 Panacea custodians, Tyler Stafford and Michael Jerkins. Nothing
                   21   herein will relieve the parties from thereafter undertaking a good-faith, comprehensive search for
                   22   documents responsive to one another’s requests for production or otherwise limiting the parties’
                   23   ability to seek relevant discovery beyond the custodians identified herein.
                   24          8.      DOCUMENTS PROTECTED FROM DISCOVERY
                   25                  a)      Pursuant to Fed. R. Evid. 502(d), the production of a privileged or work-
                   26   product-protected document, whether inadvertent or otherwise, is not a waiver of privilege or
                   27   protection from discovery in this case or in any other federal or state proceeding. For example, the
                   28   mere production of privileged or work-product-protected documents in this case as part of a mass
